orders.judge: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ravi Malimath,Sri Narayan Singh Dhanik, J.
orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND 
AT NAINITAL
Bail Application No. 620 of 2020
In
Criminal Appeal No. 297 of 2019
Arun ………….......Appellant 
 
vs. 
State of Uttarakhand …………...Respondent
Present: 
Ms. Pushpa Joshi, senior advocate, assisted by Ms. Chetna Latwal, 
advocate for the appellant. 
Mr. J.S. Virk, assistant government advocate for the State. 
Coram: Hon’ble Ravi Malimath, J.
 Hon’ble Narayan Singh Dhanik, J. 
Hon’ble Ravi Malimath.J. (Oral)
Heard learned counsels.
2. This application is filed seeking for suspension 
of sentence and bail.
3. Ms. Pushpa Joshi, learned senior counsel for the 
appellant contends that the trial court has committed an 
error in convicting the accused. The incident took place on 
21.10.2017 of an offence under Section 376 IPC, and 
thereafter she (victim) committed suicide on 23.10.2017. It 
is, therefore, pleaded that except her complaint lodged on 
the date of the alleged offence under Section 376 IPC, no 
other statement of her’s was recorded. This itself leads to a 
doubt on the entire prosecution case. It is further pleaded 
that the appellant is presently aged about 22 years and 
keeping in mind his tender age, he requires to be enlarged 
on bail. That he has been in custody since the date of the 
offence. 2
3. The same is disputed by the learned government 
advocate. He contends that a heinous offence of rape has 
been committed on the girl. She has lodged her complaint. 
She has narrated the entire incident to the police. Unable 
to bear the trauma, she has committed suicide on 
23.10.2017. There is sufficient material to sustain the 
order of the trial court. So far as the age is concerned, that 
can only be a consideration and cannot be a sole ground to 
grant bail. Hence he pleads that the application be 
dismissed. 
4. On hearing learned counsels, we do not find any 
ground to enlarge the appellant on bail. The complaint has 
been lodged by the victim herself on 21.10.2017 narrating 
the entire manner in which the incident has occurred. 
Unable to bear the trauma she has committed suicide two 
days later. The trial court having considered the evidence 
and the entire material has rightly convicted the accused. 
Prima facie, we do not find any error committed by the trial 
court that warrants interference by us at the present stage. 
5. So far as the age is concerned, it is relevant to 
notice that the appellant was aged about 19 years on the 
date the offence took place. Indeed it is quite shocking that 
a boy aged 19 years would go to the extent of committing
an offence under Section 376 IPC. Hence, we are of the 
view that so far as the contention on the age is concerned,
the same requires to be held against the appellant and not 
in his favour.
6. Under these circumstances, we do not find any 
ground to enlarge the appellant on bail. Consequently, bail 
application no. 620 of 2020 is dismissed.  3
7. Post for hearing in the usual course. 
 (N.S.Dhanik, J.) (Ravi Malimath, J.) 
 25.06.2020
Parul/k

orders.text:
CRLA No. 297 of 2019
Hon’ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
This case has been heard through video 
conferencing.
Ms. Pushpa Joshi, Senior Advocate assisted by 
Ms. Chetna Latwal, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. J.S. Virk, Deputy Advocate General with 
Mr. R.K. Joshi, Brief Holder for the State.
Miscellaneous application (IA No.5003/2020) 
is allowed. Counter affidavit filed on behalf of the 
State is taken on record.
The appellant has been convicted under 
Sections 376 and 306 IPC and has been sentenced to 
undergo rigorous life imprisonment with a fine of 
Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand only) under 
Section 376 IPC, and to undergo ten years of rigorous 
imprisonment with a fine of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five 
Thousand only) under Section 306 IPC, with default 
stipulation. 
The appellant was 19 years of age at the time 
of the incident and as of now he is 22 years of age.
A plea for expeditious disposal of the matter is 
being made by the learned Senior Counsel for the 
appellant.
Under the facts and circumstances of the case, 
we are of the view that the matter needs early 
hearing.
List this case in the first week of December, 
2020 for final hearing.
Urgency application (IA No.9579/2020) stands 
disposed accordingly.
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.) 08.10.2020

COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
Short Term Bail (IA No. 9580 of 2023)
In 
CRLA No. 297 of 2019
Hon’ble G. Narendar, C.J.
Hon’ble Ashish Naithani, J.
Ms. Chetna Latwal, learned counsel for the 
appellant. 
2. Mr. J.S. Virk, learned Deputy Advocate General
along with Mr. Rakesh Joshi, learned Brief Holder for 
the State.
3. The Application for short term bail is preferred 
seeking for release of the applicant/ convict on the 
ground that his mother needs to undergo eye operation. 
4. Learned Deputy Advocate General would take 
this Court through Rule 504 of the Uttarakhand Jail 
Manual (Rules), 2023, which deals with ‘Parole & 
Furlough’. Rule 504(ii) deals with objectives of 
releasing a prisoner on parole and furlough, and the 
same are detailed in clauses (a) to (h). Rule 504(ii)(c) 
enables the authorities to release the prisoner on parole 
or furlough to maintain and develop his self￾confidence.
5. Learned Deputy Advocate General would further 
take this Court through Rule 512 of the Uttarakhand 
Jail Manual Rules, 2023 to contend that such 
applications are to be placed before the competent 
Authority, i.e. I.G. (Prisons), and the competent  Authority is required to consider the release of the 
convict in terms of the provisions of Rule 512 of the 
Uttarakhand Jail Manual Rules, 2023.
6. In that view, the Short Term Bail Application is 
disposed of by granting liberty to the applicant / 
appellant to submit an Application to the competent 
Authority / I.G. (Prisons), and if such an Application 
for release on parole on medical ground is preferred by 
the applicant / convict, the same shall be considered 
and disposed of by the competent Authority within one 
week from the date of its receipt.
7. In the event such application is rejected, it is 
open to the applicant/ appellant to seek remedy in 
accordance with law. 
(Ashish Naithani, J.) (G. Narendar, C.J.) 
 12.02.2025 12.02.2025
